speaker: Attorney
text: Let's keep going. I want to circle back to a few things from earlier before I show you a document. Are you doing all right? Do you need water or anything?

speaker: Witness B
text: I'm fine. I have water. Thank you.

speaker: Attorney
text: Earlier you told us your sister picked you up that afternoon. About what time did she get there?

speaker: Witness B
text: Around five. Maybe a couple of minutes after.

speaker: Attorney
text: So from the time of the collision until your sister arrived, about how long was that?

speaker: Witness B
text: Twenty-five minutes, something like that. It felt longer.

speaker: Attorney
text: During those twenty-five minutes, did you stay at the store the entire time?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. I didn't leave the store property. I stayed out front.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you ever walk down the highway toward where the car ended up?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I didn't go down there. I didn't want to.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you walk down Northeast 140th Court toward the truck?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I stayed up by the store.

speaker: Attorney
text: When your sister arrived, where did she park?

speaker: Witness B
text: In the little lot by the store. She couldn't get in easy because of all the deputies' cars, but she squeezed in.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you tell her what had happened?

speaker: Witness B
text: Some. Not a lot right then. I was pretty shook up. I told her more on the drive home.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form, to the extent it calls for the content of conversations.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'm not asking what you said yet. Just whether you talked about it. You did?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, on the way home.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did your sister see any part of the collision herself?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. She wasn't there yet. She came after.

speaker: Attorney
text: Before we get to the exhibit, a few more questions about that afternoon. When the deputies arrived, about how many were there?

speaker: Witness B
text: At first one car, then more. Four or five cars, I think, and then the fire trucks and the ambulance came.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did any of them come from the west, the same direction the car had come from?

speaker: Witness B
text: Some of them did. Some came from the other way. I really couldn't tell you which ones.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were the eastbound lanes blocked off at some point?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. They put cars across the road and were waving traffic around. It got backed up up toward the hill.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see anyone take photographs or measurements while you were there?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: I saw a deputy with a camera, I think. And later somebody with a tape, a long tape, on the road. I didn't watch closely.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did anyone ask you to point anything out on the road while you were there?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. The deputy just asked what I saw and wrote it on a pad. Then he said someone might call me.

speaker: Attorney
text: And did someone call you?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, a few days later. That's when I did the written one.

speaker: Attorney
text: Where did you write it?

speaker: Witness B
text: At the sheriff's office. They had me sit at a table and write it out by hand, and then I signed it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did anyone tell you what to put in it?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. They just said write down what you saw, in your own words.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. You mentioned a deputy took your information that afternoon. Did that deputy ask you to write anything down that day?

speaker: Witness B
text: No, not that day. He took my name and number and asked me a few questions. The written one was later.

speaker: Attorney
text: And that written statement is the one we've talked about this morning, the one you reviewed before today?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. That's the one.

speaker: Attorney
text: Between the day of the collision and the day you wrote that statement, did you go back to the intersection?

speaker: Witness B
text: I drove past it. I didn't stop.

speaker: Attorney
text: Why didn't you stop?

speaker: Witness B
text: I just didn't want to. It was still too fresh.

speaker: Attorney
text: Since then, have you stopped at that store again?

speaker: Witness B
text: A few times. It's the closest store to my sister's place. I go in and out. I don't really hang around out front anymore.

speaker: Attorney
text: Has anything about the intersection changed since that day, as far as you can tell?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Foundation.

speaker: Attorney
text: Just from your own observation, driving through.

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I noticed. The road looks the same to me. Same store, same side road. I don't pay much attention to it now, honestly.

speaker: Attorney
text: Fair enough. Now, before I show you the exhibit, I want to make sure I understand some directions, so we're using the same words. The highway runs east and west there, correct?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. East and west.

speaker: Attorney
text: And the car you've described was traveling east?

speaker: Witness B
text: East. Coming from the hill side, from the west.

speaker: Attorney
text: And the truck was in the westbound lanes, in the turn lane, before it turned?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. In the turn lane on the other side of the median.

speaker: Attorney
text: And Northeast 140th Court runs which direction off the highway?

speaker: Witness B
text: South. It goes south, down past the store.

speaker: Attorney
text: And the store is on which side of 140th Court?

speaker: Witness B
text: The east side. The store's on the corner there, on the south side of the highway.

speaker: Attorney
text: When the truck turned, which direction did it turn?

speaker: Witness B
text: Left. From where it was, it turned left, across our side of the highway and onto 140th.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you say 'our side,' you mean the eastbound lanes?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, sorry. The eastbound lanes. The side by the store.

speaker: Attorney
text: No need to apologize. That's exactly why I'm asking. I'd like to show you what we'll mark as Exhibit 4.

speaker: Attorney
text: For the record, Exhibit 4 is an aerial-style map of the intersection of U.S. 27A and Northeast 140th Court. I'm handing a copy to the witness and a copy to counsel.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Thank you. I'll note for the record that this is a demonstrative and we haven't stipulated to its scale or accuracy.

speaker: Attorney
text: Understood. Ma'am, take a moment to look it over. Have you ever seen this document before today?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I've never seen this.

speaker: Attorney
text: Have you seen any map or photograph of the intersection taken from above, before today?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I remember. Maybe on a phone map, years ago, but not for this.

speaker: Attorney
text: Take your time with it. Do you recognize what's shown?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. That's the highway, going across. That's the median in the middle with the grass. And this is the crossover where the truck turned.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you see the side road, Northeast 140th Court?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, here, going down. Going south.

speaker: Attorney
text: And do you see the store?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. That's the building, here. That's the store.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you see the lanes of the highway, the two eastbound lanes and the two westbound lanes?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. Two and two, with the grass between them.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you see the crossover, the paved opening in the median?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, right here, lined up with the side road.

speaker: Attorney
text: And to the right of the store, to the east, is there anything you recognize?

speaker: Witness B
text: That's the field and the fences, going down toward where the houses are. The car went off down that way, but it's further than this shows.

speaker: Attorney
text: So the place where the car came to rest isn't on this map?

speaker: Witness B
text: I don't think so. It was way down. Past the edge here.

speaker: Attorney
text: There's an arrow in the corner of the map marked with an N. Do you understand that to point north?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes.

speaker: Attorney
text: So the top of the page is north, the bottom is south, the left side is west, and the right side is east. Is that how you understand it?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, that makes sense. The hill would be off this way, to the left, off the page.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. Is there anything on this map that looks wrong to you, compared to how you remember the intersection?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: You can answer.

speaker: Witness B
text: Not really. It's a picture from the top, so it looks different than standing there. But the road and the store look right to me.

speaker: Attorney
text: Does the map, in general, fairly show the layout of the roads and the store as they were on May 7th, 2016, as best you can tell?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Same objection. Foundation.

speaker: Witness B
text: As best I can tell, yes. The roads are where they were.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'm going to ask you to make some marks on this map. I'm handing you a pen. It's a red pen, so the marks will show up. Please don't make any marks until I ask you to. Okay?

speaker: Witness B
text: Okay.

speaker: Attorney
text: And if you're not sure about something, it's fine to tell me that instead of marking. I don't want you to guess.

speaker: Witness B
text: All right.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let's start with the truck. Before it began its turn, you said it was in the westbound left-turn lane. Do you see that turn lane on the map?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. It's this little lane right by the median, on the top side.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'm not going to have you mark that. I just want to make sure we're oriented. Now, after the collision, did the truck keep moving?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes. It kept going. It went on down the side road.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you watch it come to a stop?

speaker: Witness B
text: I saw it stopped. I saw it sitting there down the road. I don't know if I saw the exact second it stopped.

speaker: Attorney
text: Understood. How long after the collision did you notice it stopped?

speaker: Witness B
text: Pretty quick. Seconds. I looked that way and it was stopped.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you first noticed the truck stopped, were you looking south down 140th?

speaker: Witness B
text: I turned and looked that way, yes. Everybody was looking every which way. It was loud and then it was quiet.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was the truck's engine still running, as far as you could hear?

speaker: Witness B
text: I think so. I remember a rumbling for a while. I couldn't tell you when it stopped.

speaker: Attorney
text: Before the collision, as the truck began turning, was it moving in a straight line or a curve?

speaker: Witness B
text: A curve, the way you'd turn. The cab went first and the trailer swung around behind it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Using the pen, please mark where the truck came to a stop.

speaker: Witness B
text: It was down here. Down 140th, past the store. About here.

exhibit.note: B1: truck stop point on 140th Ct south of store

speaker: Attorney
text: Thank you. Would you put the number 1 next to that mark?

speaker: Witness B
text: Okay. There. Number 1.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is that mark where the front of the truck was, the back of the trailer, or somewhere in between?

speaker: Witness B
text: I was just marking the truck. Where the truck part was, the cab. The trailer was behind it, back toward the highway.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did the trailer still extend back toward the highway after it stopped?

speaker: Witness B
text: Some of it, yes. It's a long trailer. I couldn't tell you exactly how much.

speaker: Attorney
text: That's fine. Did the truck move again after that, while you were there?

speaker: Witness B
text: Not that I saw. It stayed there. The deputies were all around it after a while.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you remember anyone getting into or out of the truck?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Witness B
text: I don't remember that. I wasn't looking at it the whole time. I was mostly looking the other way, down the highway, and then at my phone calling my sister.

speaker: Attorney
text: All right. I want to go back to the moment the car reached the intersection. You've told us this morning you were outside, out front of the store. Correct?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes.

speaker: Attorney
text: About how long had you been there, outside, by the time the car reached the intersection?

speaker: Witness B
text: A good while. I'd done my shopping and come out, and I'd been waiting maybe fifteen, twenty minutes.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you standing or sitting at that point?

speaker: Witness B
text: Standing. I'd been standing a while. I had my bag at my feet.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'd like you to show us on the map.

speaker: Attorney
text: And please mark where you were standing when the car reached the intersection.

speaker: Witness B
text: I was over by the corner, near the shelter.

exhibit.note: B2: witness position at moment car reached crossover

speaker: Attorney
text: Thank you. Let the record reflect the witness has marked Exhibit 4. Would you put the number 2 next to that mark?

speaker: Witness B
text: Number 2. Okay.

speaker: Attorney
text: And would you put your initials and today's date at the bottom of the page?

speaker: Witness B
text: Here?

speaker: Attorney
text: Anywhere at the bottom is fine.

speaker: Witness B
text: Okay. Done.

speaker: Attorney
text: Were you in that same general spot the whole time the car was approaching, from when you first saw it?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Compound.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'll rephrase. From when you first noticed the car until the collision, did you move from where you were?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I was just standing there waiting. I wasn't walking around.

speaker: Attorney
text: Thank you. At this time I'll offer Exhibit 4, as marked by the witness, into the record.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: No objection to it being attached to the transcript, subject to the objection I made earlier as to scale and accuracy.

speaker: Attorney
text: Understood. I'll pass the witness. Counsel, do you have questions?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Just a few. Ma'am, I represent the motor carrier. I'll be brief. You understand you're still under oath?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Before today, had anyone shown you Exhibit 4?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Today's the first time.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: When you made the marks on Exhibit 4 a few minutes ago, did anyone help you decide where to put them?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nobody helped me. I did it myself.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Did anyone point to a spot on the map or suggest a spot to you, either today or before today?

speaker: Witness B
text: No.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Did you discuss with anyone, before today, where you would mark on a map?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I didn't know there was going to be a map.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: The mark you labeled number 2. How sure are you of that spot?

speaker: Witness B
text: Roughly, yes. I'm sure of it roughly. I wasn't measuring where my feet were. But that's about where I was.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Could you have been a few feet one way or another from that mark?

speaker: Witness B
text: A few feet, maybe. It's a little mark on a big picture. But that's the area.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: And the mark you labeled number 1, for where the truck stopped. Same question. How sure are you of that one?

speaker: Witness B
text: About the same. That's about where it was. I wouldn't swear to the exact foot.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: You'd never seen a picture of the intersection from above before today, correct?

speaker: Witness B
text: Correct.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: So you were translating what you saw standing on the ground onto a picture from overhead.

speaker: Attorney
text: Object to form.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: You can answer.

speaker: Witness B
text: I guess so. But I know that corner. I've been to that store a hundred times.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Before today, did you ever go back and stand in the spot you marked, to check what you could see from there?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. I never did anything like that.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Has anyone, an investigator or anyone else, asked you to go out to the intersection with them?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Nobody's asked me to do that.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Did you bring any notes or drawings with you today?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Just my glasses and my water.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: You mentioned earlier you wear reading glasses. Were you wearing them when you marked the exhibit?

speaker: Witness B
text: Yes, to see the little lines on the map. I don't wear them for distance. I didn't have them on that day outside.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Understood. Last thing. Other than your written statement and what you've told us here today, have you given any other statement about what you saw, written or recorded?

speaker: Witness B
text: No. Just the deputy that day, and the written one, and today.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Thank you, ma'am. I have nothing further.

speaker: Attorney
text: Nothing further from me either. Thank you for your time today. I know this hasn't been easy.

speaker: Witness B
text: Thank you.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: We'll read and sign, as we stated at the beginning.

speaker: Attorney
text: So noted.

speaker: Videographer
text: This concludes the videotaped deposition of Witness B. The original exhibit will be retained by the court reporter. We are going off the record. The time is 11:22 a.m.
